paragraphs.text: Refuses Git inside a Jujutsu workspace and hands the model jj commands instead. Jujutsu-native VCS &
version control for the DeepSeek Harness.

dsh-jujutsu
Jujutsu for DeepSeek Harness
Makes the harness jj-native — the agent uses jj instead of
Git, and is told why.

Inside a Jujutsu workspace the agent stops reaching for Git
and uses `jj` instead — and it is _told_
why, rather than just being blocked.

- **Refuses Git where it would mislead.** `git status` in a colocated repo
reports a different state

than `jj status`. The guard catches that and hands
back the command to run instead.
- **A tiered `j

j` tool surface** — 28 tools by default, with `core` (14) and
`minimal` (5) for smaller prompts — so

the model can read and write history
without shelling out and parsing output.
- **Teaches the model

** what `jj` is: no staging area, `@` is always a commit,
change IDs survive rewrites.
- **A setting
s panel**, on the plugin's own page.

The plugin is invisible outside a Jujutsu workspace, unless you turn on _Force
Jujutsu_ (then it ref

uses `jj` there and names the init command). In a plain Git
repo it otherwise does nothing at all.
## Install
Install from the harness **Plugins** page, or:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then open **Plugins → Jujutsu** to configure it. It works out of the box; the
defaults are chosen to

**Plugins → Jujutsu** to configure it. It works out of the box; the
defaults are chosen to be safe.
### Requirements
| `jj`      | **Required.** 0.46.0 or newer. `brew install jj`

|
| `jj-hunk` | Optional. Adds hunk-level `split`/`squash`. Without it those two tools report
unavailable rather than failing. `cargo install --git https://github.com/laulauland/jj-hunk --tag v0

.5.1 jj-hunk` |
| Node      | 24 or newer
## What it does
### Refuses Git, and says what to run instead

The refusal is **translated, not templated**: the guard parses the command you
actually typed and ha
nds back the exact `jj` command it maps to.
| You run                  | What happens
| What happens                                                                      |
| `git log --oneline -6`   | `Refused: git log --oneline -6. Run: jj log -r ::@ --limit 6 --no-graph

`          |
| `git diff HEAD~1`        | `Refused: git diff HEAD~1. Run: jj diff --from @-`

|
| `git push origin main`   | `Refused: git push origin main. Run: jj git p

ush --remote origin --bookmark main` |
| `git status`             | `Refused: git status. Run: jj st

atus`                                             |
| `git add src/a.ts`       | Refused with the re

ason instead of a command: there is no staging area to add to  |
| `git status --porcelain` | The ca

talogue wording — flags that change the command are never silently dropped  |
| `git rebase -i`

| Refused — it needs a terminal. Suggests `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, `jj absorb`     |
| `rm -rf
.git`            | Refused, and explains that `jj`'s commit objects live there

|
| `jj status`, `jj log`, … | Run normally

|
| `echo "git commit"`      | Runs — it never touched Git

Three rules make the translation safe to paste: Git revisions are rewritten into
revsets (`HEAD~2` →

`@--`, because `HEAD` is not a `jj` revset), anything that
does not map exactly falls back to the c

atalogue wording rather than a
half-translated command, and every argument is shell-quoted.

Reads and writes are configured separately. A user who is happy to let the model
_look_ with Git has
not thereby agreed to let it _write_.
### The `jj` tools

The default `full` surface is 28 tools; the settings page can select `core`
(14) or `minimal` (5). E

very one returns **structured JSON**, never prose, and
revisions are addressed by **change ID**, whi

ch survives a rewrite — a commit ID
does not.
| Group               | Tools
| What it does                                                        |
| Read                | `jj_status`, `jj_log`, `jj_diff`, `jj_show`, `jj_file`, `jj_evolog`, `jj_op_

log` | Working copy, history, one revision, files at a revision, evolution |
| Author              |
`jj_new`, `jj_commit`, `jj_describe`, `jj_edit`, `jj_squash`, `jj_bookmark`      | Start, commit, s

plit, reword, resume, fold, name                    |
| Hunks               | `jj_hunk_list`, `jj_hu
nk_apply`                                                  | Select and apply individual hunks

|
| History / recovery  | `jj_history`, `jj_op`, `jj_op_restore`, `jj_r
epair`                              | Rebase, duplicate, revert, abandon, restore, undo, converge

|
| Workspaces / verify | `jj_workspace`, `jj_test`

| One workspace per agent; isolated test, run, bisect                 |
| Publish / hyg
iene   | `jj_publish`, `jj_fix`, `jj_sparse`                                              | Push/fet

ch/tags (gated), format the stack, sparse patterns          |
| Coordination        | `jj_coordinate
`, `jj_group`, `jj_doctor`, `jj_sign`                              | Plan/merge/squash agent groups;
readiness report; signing           |

Reads pass `--ignore-working-copy`, so a history read never snapshots another
agent's half-written f

iles. `jj_status({snapshot:true})` is the explicit
checkpoint and the only read that writes.
### What is verified, and how

Every claim about the harness was read from the `0.2.0-rc.2` source with line
citations (docs/11); e

very claim about
`jj` was measured against the installed 0.46.0 (docs/13).
Both documents record wha
t the sweeps did **not** find, and what remains open.

The guard, the jj tools, the prompt injection and the panel have all been
observed working in a live
session. **383 tests**, `pnpm run ci` green.
